items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: The interviewee mentions John Coltrane only in the context of the interviewer's statement about young people's misconceptions regarding jazz history; the interviewee does not describe any personal interaction or relationship with Coltrane.

ctx.x: camp is, as she’s created, keepers of the flames. They’re the kids that are going out there, now Nicholas Payton or Trombone Shorty, guys like that that come up from New Orleans, they were all inspired by Louis. You can’t do anything in music that Louis hasn’t played.
As some of the people I’ve talked to complain that some of the young people think that jazz history started with John Coltrane you know.

Well those kids don’t live in New Orleans obviously. You know if you were to ask young people about, well some of them really know about Buddy Bolden, you know, and those guys in that era. But in New Orleans if you were to ask some that maybe hadn’t been studying it they will tell you that Louis Armstrong was the first one. And that is the real unique thing about New Orleans is we know the history of the music.
